title: Seeds, batches and variations in video
hook: The seed fills one block of noise in memory order: why a different frame count is a different video, why batch items can be redone alone, and why a blended noise must be rescaled.

verified.claim: prepare_noise seeds the CPU generator and draws one block for the whole latent, then converts the dtype.
LatentFromBatch writes batch_index, and LatentBatchSeedBehavior fixes or removes it.
Ancestral samplers' per-step noise comes from default_noise_sampler, on the latent's device. The plain dpmpp_sde, dpmpp_2m_sde and dpmpp_3m_sde use BrownianTreeNoiseSampler with cpu=True.
The lab reproduced prepare_noise on this PyTorch build and printed the tables.
The real prepare_noise with LatentFromBatch's batch_index gave back item 2 for item sizes that are multiples of 16, and not for others, including a 12-channel latent of 61 x 105.
Ge et al. report a designed noise prior beat a naive one when finetuning an image model for video.
The graph passes validate_prompt with file menus skipped.

unchecked: Seeds that differ by 2^32 giving the same noise is observed on this PyTorch build's CPU generator. We did not read the cause in PyTorch's source.
Item i of a batch matching the i-th draw held only for item sizes that are multiples of 16 in the lab. We did not find out why, so it's stated as seen.
Ancestral per-step noise on a GPU comes from a different generator, and we did not test it.
